stemMd: The passage supports which of the following statements about the recovery of hominin DNA from cave sediments?
instructionsMd: Consider each of the three choices separately and select all that apply. There is no credit for a partially correct selection.

options.label: A
options.textMd: It requires substantially larger samples than the sequencing of skeletal material does.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It can indicate that hominins were present at a site from which no hominin skeletal material has been recovered.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Its evidential value depends on how far the deposit sampled has escaped later disturbance.

explanationMd:
On a select-all-that-apply item, treat each choice as its own true-or-false question against the text. There is no credit for a partially correct selection, so a choice you cannot anchor to a line of the passage must be left unselected.

**Choice B — supported.** The first paragraph ends: "Several caves that have never yielded a hominin bone have now yielded hominin DNA." A cave that has never yielded a hominin bone is precisely a site from which no hominin skeletal material has been recovered, and the DNA found there is evidence that hominins were present. Note the modest verb *indicate*: the passage would not support a choice saying the method *proves* occupation, because the second paragraph is devoted to reasons for caution. **Select B.**

**Choice C — supported.** The second paragraph opens, "The promise rests on an assumption: that DNA found in a given layer entered it when that layer formed," and then lists percolating water, burrowing animals and later pit-digging as things that break the assumption. If a sequence from a layer dated to sixty thousand years ago "may in fact have arrived there much later," then what the DNA is worth as evidence turns on whether the deposit was disturbed. That is what C says. **Select C.**

**Choice A — not supported.** The passage gives one figure for sample size: sequencing "needs only a few grams of dirt." That is an absolute statement, not a comparison, and the passage never says how much bone a conventional sequence requires. With no second figure in the text, no comparison of sample sizes can be drawn. **Leave A unselected.**

**The answer is B and C.**

**How to check:** for each choice you select, name the sentence that licenses it, and for each choice you reject, name what the passage would have had to say and does not. Here B rests on the last sentence of paragraph 1 and C on the first sentence of paragraph 2, while A fails because the missing term of its comparison appears nowhere in the text. If you cannot perform that naming exercise for a choice, you are guessing.

distractorRationale.a: This turns a one-sided statement into a comparison. The passage says sequencing needs only a few grams of dirt, which suggests a small requirement, and it never states any sample size for bone, so no relative claim about sample sizes can be supported - and the direction asserted here is the opposite of the impression the text gives.

accessibilityText: Question: the passage supports which of the following statements about the recovery of hominin DNA from cave sediments? Consider each of the three choices separately and select all that apply; there is no credit for a partially correct selection. Choice A, it requires substantially larger samples than the sequencing of skeletal material does. Choice B, it can indicate that hominins were present at a site from which no hominin skeletal material has been recovered. Choice C, its evidential value depends on how far the deposit sampled has escaped later disturbance.

provenance.notes: Original item written against the original passage gre-rc-cave-sediment-dna-003. Uses the GRE select-one-or-more format with three choices, scored all-or-nothing. Not adapted from any ETS item.

review.author: gre-topup-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: B: 'Several caves that have never yielded a hominin bone have now yielded hominin DNA' states it directly. C: para 2 makes the evidential value turn on whether the layer was disturbed by percolation, burrowing or later digging. A fails twice over - the passage says sequencing 'needs only a few grams of dirt' (small, not large) and it never compares sample sizes with skeletal sequencing at all.

review.notes: Uniqueness argument: B is licensed by the final sentence of paragraph 1 and C by the opening assumption of paragraph 2 together with the disturbance mechanisms. A is unsupportable because the passage supplies no sample size for bone sequencing, so its comparison has no second term. B was deliberately worded with 'indicate' rather than 'prove' so that paragraph 2's cautions do not make it overreach. Awaiting blind independent solve; author must not publish own work.
